title: Thoughts on Traveling
content_text:
Thoughts on Traveling

Earlier, I posted a photo essay called “Nine Pictures”, and to my surprise, many people online seemed to like it.
It made me wonder — do they like the beautiful scenery of distant places, or the short story told through my words?
That thought gave me an idea: maybe I could revisit my motorcycle journey by writing short essays with photos.

But when I looked through my hard drive, I realized most of the videos I had were just clips of me riding on the road.
The scenery was still stunning even now, but it lacked stories and reflection.
So that idea quickly faded away.

During my trip, I deeply felt that a person should not only travel thousands of miles but also read thousands of books.
These two things can go hand in hand — there’s no strict order.
After riding for tens of thousands of kilometers and seeing countless beautiful views, I began to feel a sense of emptiness.
Those landscapes didn’t belong to me. I didn’t truly understand those places — I was just a passerby.

Later, a colleague from Leshan, Sichuan, suggested that I visit her hometown to try some local food.
So I rode my motorcycle there.
The cold wind on the way was biting, and I almost wanted to give up.
But since I had already come that far, I decided to stop by Meishan, a city along the way.
Only after arriving did I realize — this is Su Shi’s hometown!
In that moment, the spiritual world I’d read about in books connected with the physical world before my eyes.
It felt magical.
I think only this kind of connection can dissolve the emptiness I mentioned earlier.

So next time I travel, I’ll visit places that appeared in the movies or books I love.
